claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at elevated temperatures.
Selective laser melting can fabricate HfMoTaTiZr with a designed periodic closed-cell lattice.
Periodic closed-cell porosity removes noncritical material volume and reduces the component's overall density.
The lattice retains load-bearing pathways despite the removal of material.
The periodic lattice redistributes applied load sufficiently uniformly to preserve mechanical performance.
Eliminating redundant volume preserves the alloy's intrinsic strength.
Eliminating redundant volume preserves the alloy's creep resistance.
HfMoTaTiZr has an underlying BCC phase.
The BCC phase of HfMoTaTiZr is stable at high temperature.
The BCC phase will be retained after selective laser melting and introduction of the lattice architecture.
The lattice-engineered component will have significantly lower overall density than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The lattice-engineered component will have yield strength comparable to the as-cast alloy at room temperature.
The lattice-engineered component will have yield strength comparable to the as-cast alloy at approximately 1000 °C.
The lattice-engineered component will have ductility comparable to the as-cast alloy at room temperature and approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed architecture is applicable under structural mechanical loading from ambient temperature to approximately 1000 °C, provided stress concentrations are avoided.
A reduction greater than 20% in yield strength, ductility, or creep resistance at either test temperature is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed and the predicted outcome calls them comparable to the as-cast alloy, but the rejection rule permits losses of up to 20% without falsification.
